newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to decide PBK sell-off adviser in November.
newsitem.headline: Poland to decide PBK sell-off adviser in November.

text.p: Poland will likely pick in November the privatisation adviser for Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK) from the five consortia bidding for the job, the head of the PBK's tender commission said on Thursday.
"In November we must make the decision," Andrzej Chmiel, deputy director of the foreign department at the finance ministry, told Reuters.

Chmiel said offers from consortia led by CS First Boston, Citibank, Lehman Brothers, Access Ltd and HSBC Investment Services were in the running for the advisory role in PBK's sell-off due at the end of the first quarter of 1997.

Poland plans to complete the first stage of PBK's privatisation, which envisages selling 65 percent of the shares to a strategic investor or a consortium of institutional investors, by March 31, 1997.
It plans to offer the public at least 15 percent of the shares at a later date and give 20 percent to employees and for reprivatisation claims.
